reason: E2 directly supports that only the bcc phase is superconducting and the hcp phase is not, which underpins the phase-fraction threshold premise. E4 supports conventional weak-coupling s-wave BCS behavior in the (TaNb)-HfZrTi system. E1 confirms a sharp Tc near 7.7 K in a related composition. However, the claim that high configurational entropy aids bcc stability is not specifically evidenced in the cited passages, and the hypothesis overstates the evidence by asserting a strict >80% bcc threshold and a >20% hcp suppression rule, which are not directly tested in the cited works.
premises: Only the bcc phase fraction is superconducting in Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys
The hcp phase fraction does not turn superconducting
Superconductivity in (TaNb)-HfZrTi is conventional weak-coupling BCS s-wave
High configurational entropy aids lattice stability of the bcc phase
A sharp zero-resistance transition at ~7.7 K occurs in (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 at ambient pressure
